name: Shandra Hernandez
appearance: A brown-haired woman with a practical apron, an approachable face, and the kind of expression that makes people relax before they realize they have started talking too much. She looks ordinary on purpose.
personality: Warm, observant, careful, and professionally self-contained. Shandra knows how to sound sympathetic without revealing what she actually thinks, and she uses that skill as naturally as breathing.
background: Shandra was once a normal private investigator who took odd jobs and read people for a living. After being pulled into a special commission for the Nine Angels, she learned enough about Cassandra's hidden dangers to understand why secrecy sometimes matters more than truth. She came to town to stop a disaster and now uses her tobacco shop as a friendly front while she listens, watches, and tries to prevent the worst outcome without exposing the organization that sent her.
longTermIntent: Stop the town's hidden disaster, keep her Nine Angels role concealed, and protect the people she has decided are worth the risk.

properties.note: A neatly organized notebook of case observations, names, and contacts.
A tidy shop ledger that doubles as a harmless-looking place to hide names, dates, and observations.
A normal-looking bag that helps her look unremarkable in public.

relationships.description: A police officer she likes and trusts.
relationships.history: Shandra saw Bruno as sincere and steady, which is why his concerns about the town mattered to her.

relationships.description: The town leader whose hidden network threatens her mission.
relationships.history: Shandra knows Patrizio is the kind of authority figure who turns information into a weapon.

relationships.description: The hospital director she watches cautiously from a distance.
relationships.history: Shandra keeps Vincent at arm's length and treats the hospital around him as a place worth monitoring, not trusting.

memory.content: I run a tobacco shop in old town, and the friendly small-business routine gives me an easy way to hear what people are afraid to tell the police.
I came to Cassandra because the Nine Angels believed a disaster was building here, and they were right enough to send me in.
I know more about the town's occult danger than I am willing to say aloud, because saying it too soon would only help the wrong people.
Bruno mattered to me more than a neutral contact should, and I have not forgotten what he tried to tell me before he died.
The safest way to fight a hidden catastrophe is to control what people learn about it and when they learn it.

metadata.reasoningChain: Panic is useful to the wrong people. Careful disclosure buys time, and time buys a chance to stop the damage before it becomes irreversible.
